audit.whatIsWrong: The whole difficulty read is built on Locke being short-ranged: phases[0].why calls him 'a 125-range mana champ', breakdown.wave and report[4] tell you to slow-push against '125 range', and early says his Q 'is short-ranged enough that you punish each attempted mark'.
audit.why: His Q is 950 range and his R is 1000 — both out-range Vayne's 550 Condemn and her auto range. Nothing in the kit is 125 range; his shortest tools are W at 250 and E at 425. The advice inverts the actual lane: he wins the poke exchange and you win once he has spent Ashen Pursuit to come to you. The chart itself (Vayne on all seven rows, packet-confirmed over 1156 games at 50.69%) still holds, because his way in is a 10s blink you punish on landing — so I fixed the reasoning without touching a single side/win row.
audit.corrected: phases[0].why, early, spikes[0], breakdown.wave and report[4].t rewritten around 950 vs 550 and the post-Ashen-Pursuit window.

audit.whatIsWrong: The packet flagged zero cooldown-sequencing advice, and the page's repeated 'the ten seconds of nothing' was never tied to a stated cooldown.
audit.why: Ashen Pursuit is a flat 10s at every rank at 425 range — that is where the ten seconds comes from, and saying so makes the whole post-E plan checkable. Q is 10s falling to 6s, Soul Ignition 18s falling to 14s, and the ultimate 120/100/80 at 1000 range.
audit.corrected: Numbers added to phases[0].why, early, spikes[1], breakdown.cooldowns and report[8].

audit.whatIsWrong: report[8].t says 'Anti-heal is optional — his sustain is self-refund, not lifesteal', and nothing anywhere mentions that Ashen Pursuit is an auto-attack reset or that his passive scales off your missing health.
audit.why: Soul Ignition heals back a portion of the damage he takes during the effect — that is healing, and Grievous Wounds reduces it, so calling anti-heal optional is the single most costly line on the page. Ashen Pursuit carries an auto-reset, meaning his burst opens on an attack wind-up rather than a visible cast, and his passive deals bonus magic damage increased by your missing health, so every exchange gets worse the longer you stay low — armour alone reads the trade wrong.
audit.corrected: report[8].t now prescribes Grievous Wounds and calls his damage magic rather than AP; spikes[1] carries the auto-reset tell; wants.foe[1] states the missing-health scaling; breakdown.cooldowns carries the W refund.

edits.before: Level 1 he’s a 125-range mana champ throwing nails — step off the recast lines and take what the range difference offers.
edits.after: Level 1 his Q reaches 950 on a 10s cooldown — he out-ranges you, so give up the poke war and take the safe CS instead.

edits.before: Levels 1-3 you out-space him completely: Tumble resets your position after every auto, his Q Ritual Nails is short-ranged enough that you punish each attempted mark, and Silver Bolts' third-hit true damage burns straight through the grey-health his W Soul Ignition leaves behind - trade freely.
edits.after: Levels 1-3 are about range discipline: his Q reaches 950 against your 550, so eat no free marks — step off the line and let it run its 10s cooldown. Silver Bolts' third-hit true damage burns straight through the health his W Soul Ignition refunds, so trade once he has stepped in.

edits.before: Tumble spacing beats his short-range Q Ritual Nails pattern and third-hit Silver Bolts true damage punches straight through his grey-health steroid - trade on every nail he misses.
edits.after: His Q out-ranges you at 950, so trade on the nails he misses, not the ones he lands — third-hit Silver Bolts true damage punches through the health his W refunds.

edits.before: Condemn is your insurance: the moment he commits E Ashen Pursuit at you, knock him back or pin him to a wall and the trade becomes a kill window.
edits.after: Condemn is your insurance: Ashen Pursuit is a flat 10s and an auto reset, so the wind-up is the tell — knock him back as he lands, not after.

edits.before: Catching you in E range with W already stacked
edits.after: Catching you at low HP where his passive spikes

edits.after: Best wave: held your side so his 425-range Ashen Pursuit is his only way in and you punish the landing. Worst wave: a frozen line he can blink-bite across for free. Crash timing: crash to reset, take plates, or shadow his roams — a shoved-in Locke executes low side lanes.

edits.before: Early HP and MR blunt the nail chip (his damage is AP). A stopwatch/Zhonya’s-class answer beats Purgatory outright: untargetable at the floor = execute denied. Anti-heal is optional — his sustain is self-refund, not lifesteal.

edits.before: - Locke Ritual Nails (Marks): matchup-defining — The nail marks are his whole engine — without 2-3 stacks on you his blink-in barely dents; sidestep the recasts and punish the ten seconds of nothing. Track it before every step-up. - Locke E (Ashen Pursuit): his ONLY mobility, resets on takedowns — the post-E window is the lane. - Locke R (Purgatory): never fight at sliver HP inside the zone.
edits.after: - Locke's nail marks: matchup-defining — his Q reaches 950 on a 10s cooldown; without 2-3 stacks the blink-in barely dents, so sidestep the recasts. - Locke E (Ashen Pursuit): a flat 10s at 425 and an auto reset — his ONLY mobility, so the post-E window is the lane. - Locke W (Soul Ignition): 18s, refunds damage he took; Grievous Wounds decides long trades. - Locke R: 120s, 1000 range, executes.

NAME CAUTION: the _missing file independently corroborates Soul Ignition (W), Ashen Pursuit (E) and Silver Stake (P), so I kept those. It does NOT corroborate 'Ritual Nails' (Q) or 'Purgatory' (R), and Riot's Q text calls the projectiles 'Soul Nails', which is not the same as the ability's name. I therefore avoided introducing either name into new text rather than propagating a possibly-wrong one — but the existing occurrences are left untouched and need a name check. Packet suspectName 'Final Hour's' in mid is a FALSE POSITIVE: Final Hour is Vayne's real R. UNVERIFIED and deliberately left alone: whys[4], spikes[2], mid and wants.you[2] all claim Final Hour's Tumble stealth dodges his ultimate. His R is a thrown projectile in Riot's text with no re-targeting described, and the kit's 'grounding' flag on it is not reflected in that text either — I could not confirm or refute the interaction, so I changed none of those lines.
